Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.C. Kandpal,      President
       Mr. C.C. Pant,                         Member

Dated: 30/09/2011
                                 ORDER

(Per: Mr. C.C. Pant, Member):

These two appeals arise out of the order dated 18.10.2010 passed by the District Consumer Forum, Haridwar in Consumer Complaint No. 34/2010, whereby the District Forum has allowed the complaint and has directed the opposite party to pay to the complainant a sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) within a month from the date of the order.

2. Succinctly, the facts of the case are that the complainant Sh. Deep Singh had purchased a tractor bearing registration no. UA08-K-3393, from M/s Chaudhary Tractors. The tractor was financed by the State Bank of India, Laksar, District Haridwar - opposite party no. 2. The said tractor was insured with the New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - opposite party no. 1 for the period from 31.07.2007 to 30.07.2008. This tractor met with an accident on 12.01.2008 and got badly damaged. The intimation of the accident was given by the complainant to the authorised dealer, opposite parties and police Kotwali, Manglore. On receiving the intimation, the insurance company deputed its surveyor/investigator, who, after detailed investigation, assessed the loss at Rs. 25,746/-. The authorised dealer had given a bill of Rs. 79,542/- for the repair of the tractor. The complainant did not agree to the assessment of loss made by the surveyor, but the insurance company insisted the complainant to give his consent for the settled amount of Rs. 25,746/-. The complainant has alleged in his complaint that the insurance company's officials had asked an amount of Rs. 20,000/- as hush money, if he wanted to settle the claim according to the bill which is given by the authorised dealer. Since the hush money was not given, the insurance company repudiated the claim on flimsy ground that the complainant failed to provide the required documents despite various 3 letters/reminders sent to him. This led the complainant to file a consumer complaint before the District Consumer Forum, Haridwar. The District Forum, after an appreciation of the facts of the case, allowed the complaint in the above manner vide its order dated 18.10.2010. Aggrieved by the order, the insurance company - opposite party no. 1 has filed appeal no. 378/2010 before this commission. Dissatisfied with the order, the complainant has also filed appeal no. 373/2010. As both the appeals arise out of the same order, these are being disposed of by a common order.

3. We have heard the learned counsel for insurance company and the complainant and perused the material placed on record. None appeared for opposite party no. 2, i.e., State Bank of India.

4. The main argument advanced by the learned counsel for the insurance company is that the complainant did not submit the required documents inspite of sending various reminders and, thus, the insurance company has not made any deficiency in service by repudiating the claim. It was also argued that the tractor was being used for commercial purpose and as such the complaint is not maintainable under the provisions of Consumer Protection Act, 1986. In support of his contention, the learned counsel for the insurance company has pressed into service the following judgments :-

I. Jai Mehra vs. Sultan Chand & Sons (Publisher) & Ors.; 2011 (1) CPR 131 II. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Sangeeta Singh; 2010 (20 CPR 303 (NC) III. M/s Jagdamba Foods Ltd. vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.; 2010(2) CPR 36 (NC)

5. Countering the arguments, the learned counsel for the complainant stated that all the required documents were submitted not only once but time and again, as is evident from the copies of the letters placed on 4 record. The surveyor has also mentioned in his report that the required documents were submitted by the complainant and those were examined by him. The only document, which the complainant did not submit, was his consent letter for the amount settled by the insurance company on the basis of loss assessed by the surveyor as it was much less than the actual amount of the repairing bill issued by the authorised dealer. The learned counsel also submitted that the insurance company has not paid any money as yet and, therefore, the tractor, due to non-payment of the bill, is still standing in the authorised dealer's workshop and the complainant has suffered a huge loss due to non-availability of the tractor.

6. We considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurance company and the complainant. The insurance company's contention that the tractor was being used for commercial purpose is not tenable because the insurance company has failed to adduce any evidence in support of this contention. The other ground in the appeal filed by the insurance company is that the complainant did not submit the required documents and, therefore, it has not committed any deficiency in service by repudiating the claim. The said ground is also not sustainable in the light of the surveyor's report (paper nos. 25 to 28 on the record of the appeal file no. 378/2010) and complainant's letter dated 20.02.2009 (paper no. 19 on the record of the appeal file no. 373/2010). From the perusal of the surveyor's report it is evident that the surveyor had examined the original driving licence, registration certificate and had also obtained the copy of the police report. The surveyor has also stated in his report that only driver was seated in the tractor and the trailer was empty. Inspite of these facts, the insurance company had asked the complainant, vide its letter dated 05.01.2009 (paper no. 19 on the record of the appeal file no. 378/2010) to send the carbon copy of FIR, registration certificate and driving licence in original, road challan, number of passenger being carried in the tractor at the time of the accident and third party loss, if any, and his consent letter 5 for the assessed loss of Rs. 25,746/-. Such an approach of the insurance company is nothing but gross harassment of the complainant, because all these documents were submitted to the surveyor except the consent letter. With regard to the consent letter, the surveyor has clearly stated in his report that "The loss was assessed and discussed with the repairer. The insured completed required formalities up to till date after requesting him through regd. letters. The loss was also discussed with the insured but he was not agree with the assessment." (paper no. 26 on the record of the appeal file no. 378/2010)

7. Inspite of surveyor's report, the insurance company insisted the complainant time and again to send the consent letter. The last letter dated 27.02.2009 available on record is at paper no. 36 of the appeal file no. 373/2010, wherein the insurance company had asked the complainant to send his consent letter. Vide its letter dated 16.03.2009 (paper no. 37 on the record of the appeal file no. 373/2010) the insurance company has sent a notice to the complainant that if the consent letter is not sent, his claim's file will be closed. Therefore, in our view, it is a high handedness of the insurance company to force the complainant time and again to submit his consent letter for the amount as per assessment of the loss made by the surveyor. In other words, the insurance company has asked the complainant to surrender and to accept whatever the company decides to pay. The complainant had already expressed his disagreement with the loss amount assessed by the surveyor. Even then he was being asked to submit his consent letter for it. We express our displeasure over this attitude of the insurance company and it appears that the complainant's allegation that a hush money was being asked for a reasonable settlement of his claim might have some substance. But we would not like to comment on this point because it is beyond the jurisdiction of the Consumer Forum to see whether this allegation is true or not. Therefore, the insurance company's contention that the claim was repudiated on the ground that the complainant did not submit the required documents and, hence, it had not made any 6 deficiency in service by repudiating the claim is not true. Non- submission of the consent letter does not amount to non-submission of the required documents, if the complainant is not agreeable with the settled amount. The insurance company cannot force the complainant to submit his consent letter. If the complainant would had submitted such a consent letter on the insistence of the insurance company, the insurance company had taken the stand that the complainant had accepted the settled amount as full and final settlement and in that eventuality the complainant would had lost his right to file a consumer complaint for the redressal of his grievances. The judgments cited above by the learned counsel for the insurance company relate to such cases, where the documents were not submitted and in such cases, the Hon'ble National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that the insurance company has not made any deficiency in service by repudiating the claim. But in the instant case, all the necessary documents were submitted by the complainant except his consent letter. Therefore, the ratio of the reported decisions cannot be applied to the instant case.

8. As far as the loss assessed by the surveyor is concerned, we do not find it reasonable. The complainant has submitted three bills for a total amount of Rs. 79,542/- for the repair of the said tractor, which have been issued by the authorised dealer M/s Chaudhary Tractors. But the surveyor has considered only an amount of Rs. 52,127.28. After disallowing some of the amounts without giving any reason, he has assessed the loss at Rs. 25,746.84. The said tractor was a new one and was registered on 10.10.2007 with the transport department. The accident took place on 12.01.2008. Thus, it being a new tractor, the complainant is entitled to get the damages as per the bills issued by the authorised dealer. The District Consumer Forum, Haridwar, without giving any reason, has awarded the amount of Rs. 50,000/- in an arbitrary manner and, therefore, the impugned order needs to be modified. Keeping in view the attitude of the insurance company in this 7 case, as indicated above, we are also of the view that the complainant should be awarded an interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing the complaint till the date of actual payment. However, the losses occurred in profession/occupation, which in the case of the complainant is agriculture, cannot be compensated under the provisions of Consumer Protection Act, 1986. Accordingly, the appeal no. 378/2010 filed by the insurance company is liable to be dismissed and the appeal no. 373/2010 filed by the complainant deserves to be allowed and the impugned order dated 18.10.2010 passed by the District Consumer Forum, Haridwar is modifiable as indicated above.

9. Appeal no. 378/2010 filed by the insurance company is dismissed. Appeal no. 373/2010 is allowed and the impugned order dated 18.10.2010 passed by the District Consumer Forum, Haridwar is modified by enhancing the sum of Rs. 50,000/-, as awarded by the District Forum, to Rs. 79,542/-. The insurance company is also directed to pay to the complainant an interest @ 9% per annum on the said amount of Rs. 79,542/- from the date of filing the complaint till the date of actual payment. Cost made easy.

10. Let the copy of this order be placed in the file of appeal no. 373/2010. 

             (C.C. PANT)                 (JUSTICE B.C. KANDPAL)
